mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT both decline monotonically across the four weekly means (RETAIL_REC -17.7 to -22.4; TRANSIT -17.3 to -20.3), so the drop is a broad, still-accelerating mobility contraction rather than a single-week shock; that momentum carries RETAIL_REC lower over the next 28 days than its last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means fall from -17.7 (t-3w) to -22.4 (t-0w) with no rebound week
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or higher than the last 28-day mean in more than half of weeks where RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT have both fallen in three of the last four weekly prints.

mechanism_narrative: Household retention (RESIDENTIAL rising from 6.4 to 8.0) combined with outdoor-trip suppression (PARKS falling from -29.3 to -38.9) pushes consumption into the home; the joint condition, not either series alone, removes discretionary out-of-home retail trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is the only category above baseline, at +6.4 rising to +8.0
regime_hint: elevated at-home retention with suppressed outdoor activity
failure_condition: Weeks meeting RESIDENTIAL >= 7.0 and PARKS <= -35.0 are followed by a 14-day RETAIL_REC mean that is not lower than the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS falls below -37, outdoor leisure trips largely collapse and a measurable share of displaced trips converts into indoor retail-and-recreation errands (malls, cinemas, restaurants), producing a short one-week lift in RETAIL_REC before the broader contraction resumes.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS prints -38.9 at t-0w, its first crossing below -37.0
failure_condition: The week immediately following a PARKS print below -37.0 shows a RETAIL_REC weekly mean that is lower than or equal to the print at the time of crossing in most instances.

mechanism_narrative: A tightening-restrictions regime shows up first as simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES (-12.3 to -15.1) and TRANSIT (-17.3 to -20.3); RETAIL_REC follows with roughly a four-week lag as capacity limits and remote-work guidance spread, so RETAIL_REC keeps falling over the next 28 days.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each fall in three consecutive weekly prints
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each decline in three of the last four weekly means
failure_condition: In tightening-flagged weeks the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is greater than or equal to the prior 28-day mean in more than 50% of observed cases.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is a fast-moving essential-trip indicator: its steepest weekly drop in the window (-11.9 to -14.6) signals households cancelling all non-home trips, and RETAIL_REC absorbs that retrenchment with a one-week lead, keeping the four-week retail mean below its prior level.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM drops 2.7 points between t-1w (-11.9) and t-0w (-14.6)
failure_condition: Weeks in which GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 2.0 points week-on-week are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean above the preceding 28-day mean in most instances.

mechanism_narrative: Transit avoidance and residential retention reinforce each other: when TRANSIT is at or below -20 while RESIDENTIAL is at or above +7.5 in the same week, the drag on retail footfall is larger than the sum of the two effects alone, deepening the RETAIL_REC decline over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-mean <= -20.0 and RESIDENTIAL week-mean >= 7.5 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reaches -20.3 while RESIDENTIAL reaches +8.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: elevated at-home retention with suppressed outdoor activity
failure_condition: The combined-condition interaction term adds no explanatory power over the two single-series terms for the next 14-day RETAIL_REC change, or the sign of the interaction is positive.

mechanism_narrative: The decline is decelerating, not accelerating: PARKS weekly drops shrink from -5.1 to -2.5 to -2.0, and RETAIL_REC sits at a deep -22.4 with no fresh shock; absent new restrictions, this exhaustion-of-decline and low base produces a modest upward mean-reversion in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC 4-week mean below -21.0 while the PARKS week-over-week change is greater than -2.0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS week-over-week change shrinks from -5.1 to -2.5 to -2.0
regime_hint: steady state with no new restrictions
failure_condition: When RETAIL_REC's 4-week mean is below -21.0 and PARKS decelerates, the next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean fails to exceed the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The contraction is broad-based: five of six place categories printed lower weekly means at t-0w than at t-1w (only RESIDENTIAL rose). Breadth of decline across independent trip types is a persistent-regime signature, so RETAIL_REC continues lower over the next 28 days rather than reverting.
candidate_trigger: four or more of the six place categories record a lower weekly mean at t-0w than at t-1w
evidence_refs: fact:five of six categories fall from t-1w to t-0w; only RESIDENTIAL rises (7.3 to 8.0)
failure_condition: Weeks flagged as broad-based (four or more categories falling) are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean above the prior 28-day mean in more than half of instances.
